Window: since last distill (2026-09-06T14:37:29Z). Source ~/.claude/projects jsonl again held only this run's own trace (38 lines, structural blind spot already documented in AGENTS.md) -- mined backlog/journal.jsonl, `wl runs --days 7`, and git log instead. No corrections (no real user turns exist in this session's log), no 3x-repeated undocumented procedure, no rediscovery not already written down. One outcome-pattern finding, per priority 5: `wl runs --days 7` flagged the 2026-09-06T22:41:20 prioritizer run as `committed_without_journalling`, which the tool's own doc comment (added 2026-09-06) says is meant to name a real compliance gap ('a run whose output is commits rather than journal entries'). Traced it to a false positive in engine/wl.py's _commits_between(): that run's heartbeat-end commit used the message 'prioritizer: quiet run, no metadata changes needed' instead of a bare 'heartbeat: prioritizer', and the classifier matched bookkeeping only by a 'heartbeat:' message prefix, so a purely-bookkeeping commit with a more informative message got counted as unjournalled real work. Fixed by classifying on diff content (commit touches only backlog/journal.jsonl and every added line is a heartbeat event) as well as the old prefix, keeping the existing test_runs_ignores_heartbeat_commits passing (it bundles a heartbeat with an unrelated file under a 'heartbeat:' message) while adding test_runs_ignores_heartbeat_commit_regardless_of_message as a regression test for the case that was actually observed. Re-ran `wl runs --days 7` against the live journal after the fix: committed_without_journalling is now empty, confirming the false positive is gone. This is a fix to the observability tool itself, not a policy rule, so nothing was added to AGENTS.md -- the tool now correctly classifies future heartbeat-only commits regardless of message wording, which is a more general fix than telling prioritizer.md to change its commit message convention. No AGENTS.md additions, deletions, or sharpenings: the file's existing facts (conversation-blindspot, GitHub MCP availability, single-branch clone fix, autonomy=ask handling) all held up against today's activity with no contradiction. Did not act on the 2026-09-07T05:23:43 'observation' journal event (executor prompt-drift correlated with firing time slot, n=2 per slot) -- the observing session explicitly flagged it as insufficient data ('パターンと断定はしない'), it is already tracked in wl_f4b1d499 and ops/routines.md, and promoting an unconfirmed n=2 correlation to a written rule would be exactly the kind of premature generalisation ops/routines.md's own history warns against (its 'stored prompt wins' claim, later retracted for the same reason).
